summary: Bronwyn Finnigan works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She studied at Melbourne, Sydney, and Auckland (under Rosalind Hursthouse and John Bishop). She held posts at Auckland (~2008–2011), Marquette (2012–2014), and the Australian National University (from 2014).

Brook Ziporyn works in sinology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Chicago and the University of Michigan (PhD 1996). He taught at Northwestern University (~2003–2012) before joining the University of Chicago in ~2012.
Brooke Schedneck is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at Arizona State University, where she studied under doctoral supervisor Juliane Schober.
Bruce Cameron Hall is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned his PhD from Harvard University in 1980 and served as assistant editor at William & Mary (attested 1987).

Bruce Charles Williams specializes in sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Edward H. Schafer, Michael Rogers, Michel Strickmann, Barend A. van Nooten, Padmanabh S. Jaini, Akira Fujieda, and Noritoshi Aramaki.

Bruce John Stewart works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Sakya College in 1978 and earned his PhD at Columbia University under Alex Wayman, also studying under Joel Peter Brereton and Christopher S. George.

Bruce Lincoln specializes in religious studies, history/archaeology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Haverford and the University of Chicago (PhD 1976 under Mircea Eliade). He held posts at Minnesota (1976–1994) and Chicago (~1993–2018).
Bruce M. Knauft studied at the University of Michigan from ~1976 to 1983. In ~1986, he took up a post at Emory University as Samuel C. Dobbs Professor of Anthropology.
Bruce M. Sullivan works in Indology and religious studies. He studied under J. A. B. van Buitenen (~1977–1979) and held a post at Northern Arizona University from ~1989 to 2016.

Bruce Matthews works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He completed graduate studies at McMaster University (~1969–1974), was a Commonwealth Fellow at the University of Peradeniya (~1974–1975), and held a professorship at Acadia University (~1976–2006).

Bruce McCoy Owens works in religious studies and Indology. He held a post at Columbia University (attested 1988) and has served as associate professor of anthropology at Wheaton College (attested 2019).

Bruno Dagens worked in Indology and history/archaeology, studying under Colette Caillat. He held posts at the EFEO (1969), KU Leuven (1972–1977), the French Institute of Pondicherry (1977), and Sorbonne Nouvelle University (1986).
Bruno Galasek specializes in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Bonn, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Konrad Klaus (attested 2016).

Bruno Liebich worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Munich, Göttingen (Dr. phil. under Franz Kielhorn), and Breslau (Habilitation). He served as a professor at Breslau (~1901–1907, 1921–1928) and Heidelberg (~1907–1928).

Bruno Lindner worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Leipzig and under Rudolf von Roth (~1874–1877), later serving as a Privatdocent at Leipzig (1878–1919).

Bruno Petzold worked in Buddhist studies and Japanology after studying at Leipzig and Berlin. In Japan, he studied under Hikoshiro Hoshino and Daito Shimaji, and taught at the First Higher School (1917–1943), Chuo University, Rissho University, and Seikei High School.
Bruno Schindler worked in sinology and founded Asia Major in 1923. He completed his doctorate under August Conrady (~1912–1919) and later served as a Verlagslektor at Lund Humphries (~1939–1964).

Bryan D. Lowe works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Otani University and under Jacqueline I. Stone, Martin Collcutt, and others. He served as assistant professor at Vanderbilt University (attested 2017–2019).

Bryan J. Cuevas works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Emory and Virginia (PhD under Jeffrey Hopkins and David F. Germano). He held a fellowship at Princeton and became a professor at Florida State (attested 2008–2021).
Bryan W. Van Norden specializes in philosophy and sinology. He studied at Stanford University (~1985–1991) and joined Vassar College as a professor in philosophy and Chinese & Japanese in ~1996.
